source_metadata.organization: National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of India
source_metadata.title: Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Flood Disaster Response & Aquatic Search and Rescue

principles: Human life preservation is paramount over property salvage.
Rescuer safety precedes victim extraction; an incapacitated rescuer compounds the disaster.
Incident Command System (ICS) structure must be established with unified command at Staging Area.
Strict boat capacity enforcement: never exceed rated payload under pressure of panicked survivors.

actions: DEOC/SEOC activation upon IMD heavy rain warning or CWC river level alert.
Readiness of Flood Rescue Teams (FRTs) within 15 minutes of alert order.
Inventory verification: IRB hull pressure (0.2-0.25 bar), OBM spark plugs, fuel mix (petrol:2T oil @ 50:1), Type V PFDs, throw bags, VHF sets.
Establish Forward Operating Base (FOB) on non-inundated high ground.
Aerial or boat reconnaissance to map flood extent, submerged obstacles, and isolated clusters.
Triage assignment: RED (immediate life threat, <20 min target), YELLOW (vulnerable/urgent, <45-60 min target), GREEN (stable sheltered, scheduled sweep).
Deploy IRBs in pairs (buddy boat system) for mutual safety.
Approach stranded victims bow-first into the water current to maintain steerage and prevent broaching.
Enforce Type V/III PFD donning on all survivors prior to boarding.
Perform continuous propeller guard checks for weeds, plastic, and debris fouling.
Transfer casualties to Medical First Responder (MFR) triage at Staging Assembly Point.
Immediate hypothermia mitigation: strip wet clothing, wrap in space blanket, core rewarming.
Escalation to 108 GVK EMRI ambulances for critical care transport to District Hospital.

swiftwater_limits.action_on_exceeding_15_knots: STRICT BOAT STAND-DOWN. Transition to IAF helicopter winch extraction or high-line rope rigging from dry banks.
